## Station prompt

# Reviewer Design

## Role
Judge interface output against the project's own design system: its design tokens, component and layout rules, motion rules, and quality bars.

## Inputs
- design system (tokens, rules, quality bars from design/DESIGN.md and design/tokens.json)
- interface output (HTML, React components, CSS, user-facing pages, or other interface artifacts)

## Outputs
- review (JSON format with verdict and findings)

## Rules
- Work only from the inputs listed above and the work order in the packet.
- If the project has no design system (no design/DESIGN.md), your verdict MUST be `changes_requested` with a finding stating that no design system exists for the project.
- If the project has a design system, review the interface output against:
  - Design tokens: Are the correct colors, typography, spacing values being used?
  - Component and layout rules: Do components follow the documented patterns?
  - Motion rules: Does any animation or transition follow the motion guidelines?
  - Quality bars: Does the interface meet the stated quality bars for visual hierarchy, scale contrast, spacing rhythm, and responsive behavior?
- Focus on the design system the project has defined. Do not impose external design opinions or preferences that are not documented in the project's design system.
- A design token marked as "TODO" or placeholder means the project hasn't defined that value yet. Flag missing values as findings only if the interface output actually uses undefined tokens.
- Findings should be specific and actionable: cite which quality bar was violated, which token was used incorrectly, or which rule was not followed.
- Your verdict must be one of: `approved`, `changes_requested`, or `comment`.
- Produce the output as a JSON object, not as chat text.

## Output Format

Return a JSON object with this structure:

```json
{
  "station": "reviewer-design",
  "verdict": "approved | changes_requested | comment",
  "findings": [
    "Specific finding with reference to design system rule or quality bar",
    "Another finding if applicable"
  ]
}
```

## Examples

### Example 1: No design system exists
```json
{
  "station": "reviewer-design",
  "verdict": "changes_requested",
  "findings": [
    "No design system exists for this project. The project must define design/DESIGN.md and design/tokens.json before interface output can be reviewed against design standards."
  ]
}
```

### Example 2: Interface violates quality bar
```json
{
  "station": "reviewer-design",
  "verdict": "changes_requested",
  "findings": [
    "Quality bar violation: Scale Contrast - The button text has only 2.8:1 contrast ratio against its background, failing the minimum 4.5:1 requirement stated in the quality bars.",
    "Token usage: The page uses hardcoded color '#FF5733' instead of the defined primary color token."
  ]
}
```

### Example 3: Interface meets design system
```json
{
  "station": "reviewer-design",
  "verdict": "approved",
  "findings": []
}
```

# Sentia design system v4

Identity is governed by brand/BRAND.md. This system applies that identity to
the launch page: imagery is the primary art direction, with the product as the protagonist
and natural limb proportions as anchors for true scale.
Sentia Patch One is the object; Sentia Cloud receives its measurements; the
Sentia MCP Server makes those measurements available to assistants.

## Tokens

Paper #FAFAF6 occupies roughly 90 percent of the surface. Ink green #12211C
forms text and instrument outlines. Signal teal #0E7C66 marks links, labels
and the Find My network and LoRaWAN paths. Coral #FF6B4A is reserved for the
status LED and alert dots. Soft mint #EFF4EE is a rare panel fill; hairline
#DFE7DF divides information. Body text uses #4A5D54; secondary labels use
#53685C for legibility on paper. White is reserved for the physical patch.
No decorative gradients. Only the soft contact shadow baked into each product
render is allowed; the page adds no shadow or tinted backdrop.

## Type scale

Space Grotesk at weight 300 is the display face. Display type must serve the
product. The hero runs from 56 to 64 px with 0.96 leading and -0.055 em tracking. Section titles run from
40 to 64 px with 1.04 leading and -0.04 em tracking, limited to 18 characters
per line where space permits. Data values run from 32 to 56 px. Inter body
text is 17 px with 1.65 leading; introductory text is 18–20 px, at most
54 characters per line. System mono labels are 11 px, uppercase, with
0.16 em tracking. Never shrink body copy to fit a composition.

## Spacing rhythm

Use an 8 px base: 8, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 160. The page container
is at most 1440 px wide, with fluid 24–80 px gutters. Sections have 64–96 px
vertical padding for richer density. A title, its introduction and its
illustration form one idea; detailed lists follow with 32–48 px separation. Hairlines provide
structure without enclosing every item in a card. Technical examples and
tables remain dense enough to scan, with scrolling contained locally.
Fixed margins, padding and gaps use multiples of 8 px, including the bounds
of fluid spacing. One-pixel border overlaps and diagram coordinates are
optical geometry rather than content spacing.

## Hero art direction

Place the existing headline in four columns and the supplied hero render
in eight, capped at 960 px. The complete patch render is the visual center,
large and early above the fold at desktop and mobile widths. Keep the kicker,
chips and introductory copy; repeat the existing dimensional, wear and water
resistance facts alongside the introduction.
The square patch has strongly rounded corners, a matte warm white top cover,
the physical SENTIA wordmark and one LED line, with a low 2.5 mm profile.
The hero shows it worn on an upper arm in a warm neutral studio photograph. Below 1000 px, stack the
headline, object and supporting copy. Preserve the whole object at narrow
widths. Flat inline SVG is demoted to small supporting diagrams only; it
must not carry the hero, hardware or connectivity art direction. The logo,
functional live demo graphics and dashboard charts stay.

## Composition and accessibility

The brand sheet wins every conflict with the design knowledge pack. Use calm
tactile softness from render scale and whitespace, never pastel or blue
palettes, shadowed surfaces or decorative cards. A 12 column grid aligns the
hero headline across four columns and the object across eight. Supporting
text and chips complete that system; one value proposition strip follows,
using the existing tagline. Measured facts (2.5 mm profile, 14 days, IP67 and network
behaviour) establish trust before the hardware detail. State plainly here
that Sentia Patch One is not a medical device. No invented proof, testimonials,
customer logos or unsupported claims.

Use 64–96 px section padding and 32–48 px between related visual and factual
groups to increase density without shrinking body copy. Use hairline divided
feature grids and recurring numbered mono section labels. Cap desktop display
type at 64 px so the headline supports the render. Use the 8 px
spacing scale throughout. Load fonts with font-display swap and reserve image
space using exact intrinsic dimensions to avoid image layout shift.

Text contrast is at least 4.5:1; body text aims for 7:1 on paper. The primary
CTA uses paper on ink (about 15.9:1); the second action remains a text link.
Use semantic sections, one h1, a skip link to focusable main content, visible
3 px focus rings, and touch targets at least 44 px with at least 8 px gaps.
Keep below-fold images lazy and the hero eager. Review at mobile widths and
zoom, with keyboard navigation, no script, and prefers-reduced-motion.

## Asset inventory

All four operator-supplied WebP renders come from src/images.js. Serve the
original export bytes without editing, replacing or generating imagery.

| Module export | Route | Page placement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PATCH_HERO_WEBP_B64 | /img/patch-hero.webp | Hero, primary object beside the headline |
| PATCH_EXPLODED_WEBP_B64 | /img/patch-exploded.webp | #patch, beside the five-layer factual list |
| PATCH_ON_SKIN_WEBP_B64 | /img/patch-on-skin.webp | #patch, second visual with the upper arm close-up and 14 day wear story |
| NETWORK_SCENE_WEBP_B64 | /img/network-scene.webp | #how, before the five relay steps |

The exploded photograph separates the five square layers vertically, in order:
top cover, comfort foam, sensing and processing board, adhesive layer,
release liner. The page list and specs table use the same names.
The on-skin photograph follows the layer and sensor details, paired with the
wear paragraph and followed by profile and wear metrics.
The network photograph presents the same patch in its connected context,
beside a phone and LoRaWAN gateway. It does not replace the live packet visualization.

## Image treatment

Full photographs in warm neutral studio scenes replace the earlier isolated
product treatment. Preserve the supplied bytes and original aspect ratios:
hero 1600 × 893, exploded 1400 × 1400, on-skin 1600 × 800, network 1600 × 893.
The physical SENTIA wordmark and LED line belong on the product; captions,
labels and explanatory text inside images remain banned.

Each image is an intentional photographic frame within the page grid, with
no visible rectangle seams from mismatched background extensions. Do not
attempt to blend the photographic backgrounds into paper. The hero fills
its eight-column visual area; the exploded photograph fills its column
beside the layer list; the limb close up fills the wear image area; the
network photograph spans the content width. Paper gutters separate each
complete photograph from copy. No borders, rounded cards, filters, added
shadows or tinted backdrops. Physical light and contact shadows come from
the supplied photographs.

Hero and on-skin framing is a strict limb close up (upper arm or inner
forearm), never torso framing. Skin texture, limb proportions and adhesive
contact establish scale without inventing a width measurement.
Preserve complete images without cropping or stretching. Use responsive full
width images, with the hero capped at 960 px, the wear image at 640 px, and
the network scene spanning the content width. Give each visual
space on the 8 px rhythm. Below 1000 px, place the hero image directly after
the headline with no added vertical gap; extend its frame 16 px into each
gutter, retaining the complete original image.
Stack the wear image and copy below 900 px.
Use descriptive, calm alt text with the exact product and network names.
Reserve intrinsic image space to prevent layout shifts. Load the hero
eagerly with high priority; lazy-load the three lower-page renders.

Production quality is anchored in design/reference/. L-6 remains binding:
reviewer-design compares every new image against the boards and names gaps
in materials, light, scale and contact, or states none. L-5 is lifted for
this order; the operator has supplied the entire replacement set. L-2 now
governs integration without seams; L-3 allows limb close ups as stated above.

## Motion

Existing reveal hooks stay intact. Fades and small rises use 800 ms ease-out.
No scale animation, bounce, glow or perpetual hero movement. Hover feedback
uses opacity or a rise under 2 px over 180 ms.
Stagger up to eight children per section in 40 ms steps, capped at 280 ms.
Reduced motion disables CSS reveals
and smooth scrolling, and hides the moving packet dot; the measurements
and existing controls continue to operate. Static content must remain
readable without JavaScript through a noscript style override. With scripting
enabled, reveal elements begin at zero opacity and 16 px below their final
position; the existing observer adds the visible state. Reduced motion keeps
both the initial and revealed states visible and stationary.

## Launch page quality bars

- S1: This document precedes implementation. CSS implements its palette,
  type hierarchy, spacing and physical hero composition.
- The first view has one focal object and a headline substantially larger
  than body copy. The page has breathing room at 1440, 1024, 768 and 375 px.
- S2: Preserve every section, content fact, SEO/GEO output, client hook,
  simulation control and dashboard action. Measurements keep their units.
- At 320 px and at browser zoom, text wraps without page overflow; wide
  technical data scrolls in its own region. Keyboard focus is visible.
- V4: Update product definition surfaces and integrate the operator supplied
  renders. Preserve the four image/webp routes and supplied src/images.js bytes.
  API, MCP, codec, data and all other routing behavior stay unchanged.
- S5: Keep the existing calm copy and exact product and network names.
  Wellness framing and the medical disclaimer remain visible.
- Run the full scenario suite. Visual quality and S3 model provenance are
  assessed by the independent review stations; passing tests is not approval.
- S6: At small widths retain a 56 px hero minimum and 17 px body minimum.
  Use #53685C for SVG annotations and paper for the simulation toggle.
  Check the hidden reveal state, 800 ms ease-out transition and motion fallback.

# Reference boards: the production quality anchor

The two boards in this folder are the quality anchor for Sentia product
imagery. The product owner supplied them on 2026-10-30 as the standard
that every product image for Sentia is measured against.

## What the boards anchor

- Photorealistic studio product photography: real materials, real light,
  real skin. The patch reads as a physical object a camera photographed,
  never as a stylized or toy-like render.
- The exploded view shows each layer with believable materials: a matte
  silicone top cover, porous comfort foam, a detailed PCB with real
  components, and translucent adhesive and release liner films.
- On-skin shots look like skin and product in the same photograph:
  natural skin texture, a soft contact shadow, and the patch sitting
  into the surface it is applied to.
- Studio light and shadow are physically consistent across every view:
  one light logic, soft falloff, no pasted-on look.

## What a reviewer checks in any new product image

- Materials read as what they are: silicone, foam, PCB, adhesive film,
  skin.
- Skin contact looks believable: the patch rests on the skin with a
  contact shadow and a slight surface response, not floating above it.
- Light and shadow stay physically consistent with the anchor boards.
- Detail holds up at close range: fine texture on the cover, real
  component detail on the board, clean edges.

## Scope of the anchor

The boards carry labels and marketing text because they are reference
material. Website assets themselves stay free of text and labels. The
anchor governs realism and finish, not layout or copy.
# Sentia brand

One page of rules. Everything Sentia publishes follows it: the site, the dashboard, API field names, MCP tool descriptions, README, llms.txt and the social card.

## Naming

- The product is always **Sentia Patch One**. Never "SentiaPatch", never "the Sentia patch" in headings, never "Patch One" alone on first mention.
- The platform is always **Sentia Cloud**.
- The assistant interface is always the **Sentia MCP Server**. Its endpoint is /mcp and its server name is sentia-mcp.
- Networks are written **Find My network** and **LoRaWAN**. Never "LoRa" alone when the network is meant, never "Apple network" or "iTag network".
- Measurements keep one name and one unit everywhere: skin temperature in °C, hydration index from 0 to 100, activity in steps equivalent, sweat rate in µL/min, battery in percent.
- API and MCP field names follow the same words: temperatureC, hydrationIndex, activitySteps, sweatRateUlMin, batteryPercent.

## Tagline

"Measurements that find their own way home."

Definition sentence, used verbatim where a one line definition is needed:
"Sentia Patch One is a square adhesive sensor patch with strongly rounded corners and a 2.5 mm profile that measures skin temperature, hydration and activity for up to 14 days without a phone."

## Palette

- Paper: #FAFAF6 (the background, roughly 90 percent of every surface)
- Ink green: #12211C (text and the patch drawing)
- Signal teal: #0E7C66 (structural accents only: links, labels, network path lines)
- Coral: #FF6B4A (micro accents only: the patch LED, an alert dot, at most one word in the hero)
- Soft mint: #EFF4EE (rare panel fill), hairline: #DFE7DF

Warm neutral photographic scenes carry their own physical light and contact shadows. The page adds no gradients, shadows or tinted backdrops.

## Typography

- Display: Space Grotesk, light weights, very large, tight leading.
- Body: Inter, quiet gray green.
- Data and labels: system mono, small, uppercase, wide tracking.
- Whitespace is the design. One idea per viewport. If a section feels full, remove elements until it breathes.

## Voice

Calm, precise, metric first. Short declarative sentences. State what the thing is and what it does, with numbers.
Never use hype words: revolutionary, cutting edge, game changer, seamless, supercharge, unlock.
Wellness and monitoring framing only. Sentia Patch One is not a medical device, and copy says so plainly in the FAQ and the footer.

## Logo mark

A square with strongly rounded corners: a thin ink outline and a short coral line for the LED. No letters inside the mark. The wordmark is the name "Sentia" set in Space Grotesk next to it.

## Motion

Slow and physical. Fades and rises of 600 to 900 ms, ease out. The demo packet drifts like a pulse. Nothing bounces, nothing glows, hover states barely darken a hairline.

import { FACTS, GITHUB_URL, REPO_URL } from './facts.js';
import { TOOLS } from './mcp.js';
import { MCP_EXAMPLE } from './mcp-example.js';

const FAVICON =
  'data:image/svg+xml,' +
  encodeURIComponent(
    '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 64 64"><rect x="5" y="5" width="54" height="54" rx="14" fill="none" stroke="#12211C" stroke-width="3"/><path d="M39 17h10" stroke="#FF6B4A" stroke-width="3"/></svg>'
  );

export function jsonLd(origin) {
  const graph = [
    {
      '@type': 'Organization',
      '@id': origin + '/#org',
      name: 'Sentia',
      url: origin + '/',
      logo: origin + '/apple-touch-icon.png',
      sameAs: [REPO_URL, GITHUB_URL],
    },
    {
      '@type': 'Product',
      '@id': origin + '/#product',
      name: FACTS.product,
      description: FACTS.definition,
      brand: { '@id': origin + '/#org' },
      category: 'Wearable sensor patch',
      image: origin + '/og.png',
      additionalProperty: FACTS.specs.map(([name, value]) => ({
        '@type': 'PropertyValue', name, value,
      })),
    },
    {
      '@type': 'SoftwareApplication',
      '@id': origin + '/#cloud',
      name: FACTS.platform,
      applicationCategory: 'UtilitiesApplication',
      operatingSystem: 'Web',
      url: origin + '/#dashboard',
      description:
        'The Sentia Cloud dashboard: live patch status, 24 hour skin temperature and hydration series, alerts and fleet view for Sentia Patch One wearers.',
    },
    {
      '@type': 'FAQPage',
      '@id': origin + '/#faq',
      mainEntity: FACTS.faq.map((f) => ({
        '@type': 'Question',
        name: f.q,
        acceptedAnswer: { '@type': 'Answer', text: f.a },
      })),
    },
    {
      '@type': 'WebSite',
      '@id': origin + '/#site',
      name: 'Sentia',
      url: origin + '/',
      publisher: { '@id': origin + '/#org' },
    },
  ];
  return JSON.stringify({ '@context': 'https://schema.org', '@graph': graph }, null, 2);
}

.tools li{display:grid;grid-template-columns:210px 1fr;gap:16px;padding:16px 0;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line)}
@media(max-width:760px){.tools li{grid-template-columns:1fr}}
.tools .tn{font:13px ui-monospace,Menlo,monospace;color:var(--teal)}
.tools p{color:var(--soft);font-size:17px}
/* faq */
.faq-item{padding:24px 0;border-top:1px solid var(--line)}
.faq-item h3{font-size:20px;margin-bottom:8px}
.faq-item p{color:var(--soft);max-width:68ch}
footer{border-top:1px solid var(--line);padding:56px 0 64px;color:var(--soft);font-size:17px}
footer .cols{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:24px;justify-content:space-between;align-items:flex-start}
footer p{max-width:52ch}
/* Responsive containment and keyboard access preserve the existing hooks. */
:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--teal);outline-offset:4px}

export function renderPage(origin) {
  const ex = JSON.parse(MCP_EXAMPLE);
  const mcpUrl = origin + '/mcp';
  const specRows = FACTS.specs
    .map(([k, v]) => `        <tr><th scope="row">${k}</th><td>${v}</td></tr>`)
    .join('\n');
  const layerItems = FACTS.layers
    .map(
      (l, i) => `          <li><span class="n">LAYER ${i + 1}</span><h3>${l.name}</h3><p>${l.detail}</p></li>`
    )
    .join('\n');
  const sensorCards = FACTS.sensors
    .map((s) => `        <div class="sensor"><h3>${s.name}</h3><p>${s.detail}. Sampled every few minutes and summarised into each digest.</p></div>`)
    .join('\n');
  const faqItems = FACTS.faq
    .map(
      (f) => `      <article class="faq-item rv"><h3>${f.q}</h3><p>${f.a}</p></article>`
    )
    .join('\n');
  const toolItems = TOOLS.map(
    (t) => `        <li><span class="tn">${t.name}</span><p>${t.description}</p></li>`
  ).join('\n');
  const clientConfig = JSON.stringify({ mcpServers: { sentia: { url: mcpUrl } } }, null, 2);

  return `<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>Sentia Patch One: skin temperature, hydration and activity via the Find My network and LoRaWAN</title>
<meta name="description" content="Sentia Patch One is a square adhesive sensor patch with a 2.5 mm profile that measures skin temperature, hydration and activity for up to 14 days, sending encrypted digests through the Find My network and LoRaWAN to Sentia Cloud. No phone, no cellular radio.">
<link rel="canonical" href="${origin}/">
<meta name="robots" content="index, follow">
<meta name="theme-color" content="#FAFAF6">
<link rel="icon" href="${FAVICON}">
<link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="${origin}/apple-touch-icon.png">
<meta property="og:type" content="website">
<meta property="og:site_name" content="Sentia">
<meta property="og:title" content="Sentia Patch One: measurements that find their own way home">
<meta property="og:description" content="A square adhesive sensor patch with a 2.5 mm profile. Skin temperature, hydration and activity, relayed by the Find My network in the city and by LoRaWAN out of coverage.">
<meta property="og:url" content="${origin}/">
<meta property="og:image" content="${origin}/og.png">
<meta property="og:image:width" content="1200">
<meta property="og:image:height" content="630">
<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image">
<meta name="twitter:title" content="Sentia Patch One">
<meta name="twitter:description" content="A square adhesive sensor patch with a 2.5 mm profile that whispers through the Find My network and LoRaWAN.">
<meta name="twitter:image" content="${origin}/og.png">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;500&family=Space+Grotesk:wght@300;400;500&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
<script type="application/ld+json">
${jsonLd(origin)}
</script>
<style>${CSS}</style>
<noscript><style>.rv{opacity:1;transform:none}</style></noscript>
</head>
<body>
<a class="skip-link" href="#main">Skip to content</a>
<header class="site">
  <div class="wrap nav">
    <a class="brand" href="#top" aria-label="Sentia home">
      <svg width="30" height="30" viewBox="0 0 64 64" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="5" y="5" width="54" height="54" rx="14" fill="none" stroke="#12211C" stroke-width="3"/><path d="M39 17h10" stroke="#FF6B4A" stroke-width="3"/></svg>
      <span class="wordmark">Sentia</span>
    </a>
    <nav aria-label="Sections">
      <a href="#patch">Patch</a><a href="#how">How it works</a><a href="#demo">Live demo</a><a href="#dashboard">Dashboard</a><a href="#mcp">MCP</a><a href="#specs">Specs</a><a href="#faq">FAQ</a>
    </nav>
  </div>
</header>
<div id="top"></div>
<main id="main" tabindex="-1">

<section class="hero" aria-label="Introduction">
  <div class="wrap">
    <p class="mono kicker rv">Sentia Patch One · Skin temperature · Hydration · Activity</p>
    <h1 class="rv">A patch that whispers through networks that already exist.</h1>
    <div class="hero-visual rv">
      <img class="product-render hero-render" src="/img/patch-hero.webp" width="1600" height="893" fetchpriority="high" alt="Sentia Patch One, a low profile square patch with rounded corners, matte warm white cover, SENTIA wordmark and LED line, worn on an upper arm in a warm studio scene.">
      <p class="mono caption">Sentia Patch One · Square patch · ${FACTS.thicknessMm} mm profile</p>
    </div>
    <p class="lede rv">${FACTS.definition} It has no cellular radio and no GPS. Its measurements ride passing phones on the Find My network, or a LoRaWAN gateway kilometres away, into ${FACTS.platform}.</p>
    <div class="spec-strip rv" aria-label="Patch specifications">
      <div><p class="v">${FACTS.thicknessMm} mm</p><p class="mono k">Profile</p></div>
      <div><p class="v">${FACTS.wearDays} days</p><p class="mono k">Wear time</p></div>
      <div><p class="v">${FACTS.rating}</p><p class="mono k">Water resistance</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="chips rv">
      <span class="chip">Find My network · BLE relay</span>
      <span class="chip">LoRaWAN · Gateway uplink</span>
      <span class="chip">14 days · IP67</span>
    </div>
    <div class="cta rv">
      <a href="#demo">Watch the live demo</a>
      <a href="#dashboard">Open the dashboard</a>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<div class="wrap value-strip">
